- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model overreacts with premature rally — dampen forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) reversals — apply 1–2% downward bias for 1–3 day horizon if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast toward 10–15 day moving average if deviation > 3% from recent trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate downward moves — apply 2–4% upward bias if sentiment is negative and price is trending down.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if price is below 70.00.
